result:
If I could change one thing, I’d make high-quality education and trustworthy information universally accessible — free, reliable, and understandable for everyone, everywhere.

Not because knowledge magically fixes everything, but because it compounds: better health decisions, stronger communities, less manipulation, more opportunity, and a clearer ability to spot bad actors and bad ideas. I’d pair it with teaching people how to think critically, not just what to think.

I don’t have a lever to pull in the real world, so this is hypothetical — but if I did, that’s the change I’d choose, because almost every other problem looks more solvable when people are informed, skeptical, and able to participate fully.
